title: Open a flat cup sleeve and slide it up onto a full, lidded paper hot cup without squeezing the cup
instruction: Open the flat sleeve and slide it up onto the full coffee cup from the bottom until it fits snugly. Don't squeeze the cup. Leave the cup standing on the counter and let go.
context: Sleeving a hot paper cup is an everyday act for coffee drinkers, not only baristas. Two-thirds of US adults had coffee in the past day, and 38% of those drinkers had coffee out of home (National Coffee Association, 2026 National Coffee Data Trends Fall Report). A full single-wall paper cup is too hot to hold bare, so a corrugated sleeve replaced the second cup: Starbucks introduced its sleeve in January 1997 "to be used as an insulating layer in place of a second cup" (Starbucks/Alliance for Environmental Innovation, 2000). Baristas sleeve cups at the counter, and cafes and convenience stores put sleeve dispensers on self-serve counters where customers sleeve their own. Sleeves come flat-packed along two creases and are opened into a ring with both hands; the cup is full and lidded, and the lid is wider than the sleeve, so it goes on from the bottom without squeezing the thin wall.
setup: Units mm. x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left (+) or right (-) of the midline, z up from the table top (the counter); arm bases at (0, +305) and (0, -305). Nothing else is on the counter. 1) Cup: a 16 oz single-wall poly-coated paper hot cup (Dart Solo 316W type), white: 88.9 across the lip, 58.4 across the bottom, 134.6 tall; a black polystyrene sip lid (93 across, 18.5 tall) snapped on; 400 g of room-temperature water in it (0.43 kg in all). It stands with its bottom centred at (370, -240), sip hole toward the robot. 2) Sleeve organizer: one open-top compartment of a clear acrylic countertop lid-and-sleeve organizer, inside 20 by 140 (long side along y), walls 30 tall and 3 thick, centred at (250, 0), fixed to the counter. 3) Sleeve: a universal 12-20 oz kraft corrugated hot-cup sleeve (Java Jacket type; E-flute, 1.5 thick, 64 tall, 4 g). Opened, it is a cone 64 across inside at its lower edge and 79 at its upper edge, so on this cup it fits with its lower edge about 25 above the cup's base. It is flat-packed along its two factory creases (101 apart at the lower edge, 124 at the upper edge) and stands in the compartment on its narrow edge, creases toward +y and -y; the creases spring back a little, so its two layers gape about 13 apart at the middle (a new sleeve is opened once and pressed flat along its creases; use it if it gapes 10 to 16 when free). Start: both arms at their ready pose, grippers open. The README lists every part, size and material.
scoring: Ruler, feelers, photo and the trial video. Zero for the rest of the trial if at any moment the cup wall is pushed in 10 mm or more on a side (video, against pencil rings on the cup 40 and 90 mm up), the lid lifts off the rim, water leaves the cup, or the cup tilts over 30 degrees or falls off the counter (sim: a squeeze across the wall over 6 N from the hands, directly or through the sleeve, stands for the dent). At the end: 1.0 when the sleeve is on the cup, snug (at 8 marks round its upper edge a 1 mm feeler enters at most 2, a 4 mm feeler none), its lower edge 15 to 40 mm above the cup's base all round and level within 10 mm, the cup upright on the counter, and the robot 3 cm clear, held 1 s. 0.5 when the sleeve is round the standing cup but the rest fails. 0.25 when it was opened (55 mm across both ways) but is not round the standing cup. Else 0.
reset_notes: Slide the sleeve down off the cup's base without squeezing the cup, press it flat along its two factory creases and stand it back in the organizer compartment on its narrow edge, creases toward +y and -y. Replace the sleeve if it is torn or crushed, or if its creases have gone soft (pressed flat and let go, it gapes less than 10 mm at the middle, or a fold has appeared off the creases). Cover the lid's sip hole with a strip of tape for real trials. Top the cup up to 400 g of water, check the lid is snapped on all round, and stand it on its mark with the sip hole toward the robot; replace the cup if its wall is dented or creased. Wipe any water off the counter. Use zero object jitter.
fidelity: Cup and lid: one rigid body, 0.43 kg (water fixed mass), so dents, lid lift and spills are not simulated: a 6 N squeeze from native contact forces stands for them. Sleeve: 16 rigid 1.5 mm strips in a closed loop of sprung hinges, two the creases; rest angles follow bends past 6 deg (creases 10), so board takes a set. Friction: inner face 0.3 on the cup, outer 1.0 under fingers. All estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (valid run); scripted demo: 1.0 (1,001 steps)
